<!-- Generated by `lyrac doc`. Edit the `///` comments in the source, not this file. -->

The environment a program was started with — `getenv` — and the process's own id.

**A variable is `Maybe<string>`, and an empty one is `Some("")`.** POSIX lets a
variable be set and empty, which is not the same as unset: `TZ=` means "use UTC" to
some tools and "I said nothing" to none of them. Collapsing the two would make that
distinction unsayable here, so it is kept.

**Reading only.** `setenv` changes a process-wide table that the C library, the zone
reader and any thread may be looking at, so a library offering it hands its caller a
way to change another library's answers underneath it. Nothing here has wanted it.

```lyra
import std.env.{ lookup }

let home = lookup("HOME").unwrap_or("/")
```

## Functions

### `lookup`

```lyra
pub let lookup = (name: string) -> Maybe<string>
```

The value of the environment variable `name`, or `None` when it is not set.

Not `pure` and not `det`: the environment is read from outside the program, and a call
made twice may answer differently if something else in the process changed it. Read it
once at the edge and pass the value along, the rule `today()` keeps for the clock.

### `process_id`

```lyra
pub let process_id = () -> i64
```

This process's id, as the operating system numbers it (`getpid`).

Not `pure`: another run of the program is another process. A variable naming a process
— `lyrac run --live` leaves `LYRA_LIVE_PID` — is about this one only when the two agree,
since a program started from this one inherits the variable and not the id.
